items.name: Barrington Town Beach
items.blurb: Barrington's long sandy town beach faces Narragansett Bay. Seasonal swimming facilities serve both residents and visitors under the town's parking rules. Has: sandy beach, seasonal lifeguards, restrooms, showers, parking, bike racks, dogs prohibited on managed beach sand during season.
items.hours: 2026 season May 23-September 7; lifeguards 9am-5pm and facilities until 7pm. Late-season service reduced to weekends because of staffing. · 2026 parking: resident day $6; nonresident $16 weekdays or $22 weekends/holidays. Resident season $40; qualifying resident seniors no charge. Walkers and bicyclists: no charge.

items.name: Elm Lane beach
items.blurb: A public path at the end of Elm Lane reaches the bay beach. The small shoreline access includes a bulkhead used for fishing. Has: beach, no restrooms, public pedestrian access.

items.name: Mussachuck Beach (Appian Way)
items.blurb: A short land-trust path reaches a sandy point on Narragansett Bay. Wetland habitat borders the beach and offers birdwatching opportunities. Has: sandy beach, no roadside parking, no restrooms.
items.address: Located next to 61 Appian Way, Barrington

items.name: Nayatt / Daunis Road beach
items.blurb: A public path follows Mussachuck Creek toward a cobble beach on Narragansett Bay. The small access has very limited space for cars. Has: cobble beach, limited parking, no street parking.

items.name: Nayatt Point Beach
items.blurb: Nayatt Point Beach is named in the state’s coastal-barrier inventory. Current public entry arrangements have not been confirmed. Has: coastal barrier.

items.name: Rumstick Point barrier beach
items.blurb: Rumstick Point barrier beach is named in the state’s coastal-barrier inventory. Current public entry arrangements have not been confirmed. Has: coastal barrier.

items.name: Teed Avenue beach (Hundred Acre Cove)
items.blurb: A steep fenced path reaches a sand-and-cobble beach on the tidal cove. The shore can be used to launch hand-carried boats. Has: tidal cove beach, kayak launch, steep path, no street parking.
items.address: Located directly across street from 38 Teed Avenue, Barrington

items.name: Willow Way Beach
items.blurb: This neighborhood right-of-way reaches a bay beach backed by wetland habitat. The shoreline inventory identifies it as unsafe for swimming. Has: beach, swimming unsafe, no street parking, no restrooms, birdwatching.
items.address: Located next to 20 Willow Way, Barrington

items.name: Aaron Avenue cobble beach
items.blurb: A grassy opening beside the East Bay Bike Path leads to steps and a cobble beach. The shoreline provides a small access for fishing and hand-carried boats. Has: cobble beach, steps, kayak launch.

items.name: Annawamscutt Drive beach
items.blurb: A paved public approach and short stairway lead to a cobble beach on Mount Hope Bay. The shoreline has views toward Fall River. Has: cobble beach, steps, no street parking, no restrooms.
items.address: Eastern end of Annawamscutt Drive, Bristol

items.name: Beach Road cobble beach (Bristol)
items.blurb: Steps below a roadside overlook reach a narrow cobble beach. High tide can cover the beach entirely. Has: tidal cobble beach, steps, limited street parking, no restrooms.

items.name: Bristol Narrows beach and fishing area
items.blurb: A sandy peninsula and adjoining cobble shore lie near the mouth of the Kickemuit River. Dangerous water conditions make this a fishing access rather than a swimming beach. Has: sand and cobble shore, swimming prohibited, parking, no restrooms.

items.name: Bristol Town Beach
items.blurb: The town beach occupies a sheltered bay-facing shoreline near Colt State Park. Seasonal facilities include a managed swimming area and a large recreation complex. Has: beach, seasonal lifeguards, parking, restrooms, picnic areas, dogs prohibited.
items.hours: Parking year-round; seasonal gate booth 8am-4pm from Memorial Day weekend-Labor Day weekend; gates close sunset. · Resident daily parking $10 weekdays/$20 weekends and holidays; nonresident $20/$40. Eligible Bristol residents and BWRSD families: season pass $10 per vehicle. Cash only.

items.name: Camp St. Dorothy beach
items.blurb: State monitoring records identify a saltwater beach at Camp Saint Dorothy in Bristol. Current camp access and beach operations have not been confirmed. Has: camp beach.

items.name: Constitution Street beach
items.blurb: Stone steps through the seawall reach a small beach at the end of Constitution Street. The access is close to central Bristol Harbor and nearby timed street parking. Has: small beach, steps, nearby timed street parking, no restrooms.
items.address: At the end of Constitution Street, Bristol

items.name: Fales Road cobble beach
items.blurb: A concrete ramp at the end of Fales Road reaches the cobble shore of Narragansett Bay. The access is suitable for hand-carried boats rather than trailered launching. Has: cobble beach, ramp, limited street parking, no restrooms.

items.name: Halsey Chase Herreshoff Park beach
items.blurb: A broad lawn slopes toward steps and a cobble shoreline on Bristol Harbor. The upper park provides a place to picnic or watch boats. Has: cobble shore, steps, parking, no restrooms, picnic lawn.
items.address: At the intersection of Hope Street and Walley Street, Bristol

items.name: Independence Park beach
items.blurb: A small beach adjoins the launching area at Independence Park on Bristol Harbor. The park connects waterfront paths with the southern end of the East Bay Bicycle Path. Has: small harbor beach, parking, nearby restrooms, boat ramp, picnic tables, accessible park paths.

items.name: King Philip Avenue beach
items.blurb: A public grass-and-pavement approach reaches a cobble beach on Mount Hope Bay. The site has a small launching ramp and picnic table. Has: cobble beach, kayak launch, limited street parking, no restrooms.
items.address: Directly across from 25 King Philip Avenue, Bristol

items.name: Low Lane cobble beach
items.blurb: An overgrown public path leads to a cobble beach and small breakwater. The shoreline faces the upper East Passage with views toward Hog Island. Has: cobble beach, rough path, no street parking, no restrooms.

items.name: Mount Hope Fishing Access beach
items.blurb: A cobble beach and fringing marsh adjoin the state boat ramp. Swimming is prohibited at this fishing and boating access. Has: cobble beach, swimming prohibited, parking, boat ramp, no restrooms.

items.name: Old Ferry Road beach
items.blurb: A public road beside the Mount Hope Bridge ends at a cobble beach. The shoreline provides views across Mount Hope Bay and space for hand-carried boat launching. Has: cobble beach, limited timed street parking, no restrooms.

items.name: Platt Street / Narrows Coastal Access beach
items.blurb: Concrete stairs and a path descend through a small overlook to a cobble beach. Views extend across Mount Hope Bay toward Bristol Narrows and Fall River. Has: cobble beach, stairs, limited street parking, no restrooms.
items.address: At the intersection of Platt Street and King Phillip Avenue, Bristol

items.name: Portside Drive cobble beach
items.blurb: A marked public path leads from Portside Drive to a cobble beach. The shore looks over Bristol Harbor toward Hog Island. Has: cobble beach, designated parking, rocky path.

items.name: Sunrise Drive rocky beach
items.blurb: The paved street extension ends at a rocky step-down to a small beach. The shore overlooks Mount Hope Bay and the Bristol Narrows. Has: rocky beach, street parking, no restrooms.
items.address: Next to 64 King Philip Avenue, Bristol

items.name: Surf Drive beach
items.blurb: A marked town right-of-way reaches a small rocky beach near the Warren River mouth. The shoreline has views of Rumstick Point and Narragansett Bay. Has: rocky beach, limited street parking.

items.name: Union Street beach
items.blurb: A grassy public right-of-way reaches a seawall and ramp to a sand-and-gravel beach. The site provides a compact harborfront place for a picnic or hand-carried boat launch. Has: sand and gravel beach, limited parking, ramp, no restrooms.
items.address: At the intersection of Hope Street and Union Street, Bristol

items.name: Blue Shutters Town Beach
items.blurb: Blue Shutters is a town-operated ocean beach west of the Ninigret barrier. The sandy shoreline has seasonal facilities and accepts both resident and nonresident beach passes. Has: sandy beach, seasonal lifeguards, restrooms, showers, parking, concessions, dogs prohibited Memorial Day-Labor Day 9am-5pm.
items.hours: 2026 season May 23-Labor Day; 9am-5pm weekdays and 8am-5pm weekends/holidays. · 2026 parking $30 weekdays or $45 weekends/holidays; age 65+ $25/$40. Resident season $75; resident senior $35. Walk-ons: no charge. Nonresident season pass $150; nonresident senior $75.

items.name: Charlestown Breachway
items.blurb: Ocean beach and saltwater-fishing access beside the breachway.

items.name: Charlestown Breachway State Beach
items.blurb: A broad sandy beach borders the ocean beside the Charlestown Breachway. The adjacent jetty and boat launch serve a different purpose from the guarded swimming area. Has: sandy beach, seasonal lifeguards, restrooms, composting toilets, parking, accessible beach chairs, nearby boat launch.
items.hours: Year-round shore access. 2026 staffed season May 23-September 7; lifeguards 9am-6pm weekdays and 8:30am-6pm weekends/holidays, subject to staffing and weather. Age 65+: half-price. Off-season parking: no charge.

items.name: Charlestown Town Beach

items.hours: 2026 season May 23-Labor Day; 9am-5pm weekdays and 8am-5pm weekends/holidays. · 2026 parking $30 weekdays or $45 weekends/holidays; age 65+ $25/$40. Resident season $75; resident senior $35. Walk-ons: no charge. Nonresident seasonal passes not accepted.

items.name: East Beach
items.blurb: A less-developed barrier beach with limited parking and fewer facilities than the larger state beaches.

items.blurb: East Beach is a long barrier separating Ninigret Pond from the ocean. Its limited facilities and extensive dunes distinguish it from the larger developed state beaches. Has: sandy barrier beach, seasonal lifeguards, composting toilets, limited parking, permitted sand-trail vehicle access, dogs prohibited in designated swim areas April 1-September 30 except service animals, leashed dogs allowed outside that restriction.
items.hours: Year-round shore access. 2026 staffed season May 23-September 7; lifeguards 9am-6pm weekdays and 8:30am-6pm weekends/holidays, subject to staffing and weather. No lifeguards after September 7. · 2026 parking: RI vehicles $6 weekdays or $7 weekends/holidays; out-of-state vehicles $12 weekdays or $14 weekends/holidays. Season pass: RI $30; nonresident $60. Age 65+: half-price. Off-season parking: no charge.

items.name: East Pond Beach

items.name: Garden Pond Beach

items.name: Michel Pond Beach

items.name: Quonochontaug Breachway
items.blurb: The state fishing area follows the eastern side of the channel connecting Quonochontaug Pond with the ocean. items.blurb: Central Beach is maintained by the Quonochontaug Central Beach Fire District. Pedestrian access and district parking have different permit requirements. Has: no lifeguards, district-pass parking, dogs prohibited under June 2026 beach rules.

items.name: Ocean Avenue beach (Cranston)

items.address: At the southern end of Seaview Avenue, Cranston

items.name: Stillhouse Cove Beach
items.blurb: Stillhouse Cove has a small tidal shore beside its waterfront park. It is an urban shoreline access also used for launching small boats. Has: tidal cove, boat ramp, nearby street parking, no restrooms.
items.address: Located in Stillhouse Cove Park across from 1507-1543 Narragansett Boulevard, Cranston

items.name: Sabin Point Beach

items.address: At the intersection of Shore Road and Sabin Point, East Providence

items.name: Second Beachway shore

items.address: At the southern end of Beavertail Road, Jamestown

items.name: Buccaneer Way beach access
items.blurb: A grassy public path reaches the West Passage shore between Dory Street and Champlin Way. The beach provides a place to sit beside the bay or launch a hand-carried boat. Has: public shoreline access, limited street parking, no restrooms, kayak launch.

items.address: At the eastern end of Fairview Street, Jamestown

items.name: Fort Getty Beach
items.blurb: A rocky beach borders the town's former coastal fort and campground. The surrounding park also has walking trails and a public boat ramp. Has: rocky beach, parking, restrooms, boat ramp, picnic areas, dogs leashed May 16-September 30, off-leash dogs October 1-May 15 only 7am-11am and 3pm-7pm.
items.hours: Summer nonresident parking fee; resident recreation sticker required for resident entry.

items.name: Fort Wetherill coves and cobble beaches
items.blurb: Sheltered coves and cobble beaches lie below the cliffs of Fort Wetherill. The park provides shoreline access used by divers as well as paths to coastal viewpoints. Has: cobble beaches, rocky coves, parking, restrooms May 1-October 31, leashed dogs allowed, uneven beach access.

items.name: Fox Hill Pond barrier beach
items.blurb: Fox Hill Pond barrier beach is named in the state’s coastal-barrier inventory. Current public entry arrangements have not been confirmed. Has: coastal barrier.

items.name: Mackerel Cove
items.blurb: Jamestown’s town beach, suitable for a beach-and-village outing. Parking is limited and seasonal rules apply.

items.name: Mackerel Cove Town Beach
items.blurb: Mackerel Cove has a broad beach at the sheltered head of a long inlet. It is Jamestown's principal managed swimming beach. Has: sand and cobble beach, seasonal lifeguards, restrooms, paid visitor parking, resident-designated parking, dogs prohibited May 16-September 30, off-leash dogs allowed October 1-May 15.
items.address: On the South side of Beavertail Road just past Hamilton Avenue, Jamestown
items.hours: Published beach season June 18-September 7; 9am-5pm. · Day parking without resident pass: $20 per vehicle; credit/debit card payment. Resident recreation pass accepted.

items.name: Middle Street rocky beach

items.address: At the end of Middle Street, Jamestown

items.name: Park Dock Beach (Broad Street)

Has: rocky beach, resident-only parking, restroom, uneven access, dogs allowed off leash October 1-May 15, May 16-September 30 dogs allowed only 6am-10am and 5:30pm-sunset.
items.address: At the eastern end of Broad Street, Jamestown

items.name: Potter Cove Beach (Taylor Point)

items.name: Briggs Beach

items.blurb: Round Pond Beach is named in the state’s coastal-barrier inventory. Current public entry arrangements have not been confirmed. Has: coastal barrier.

items.name: Sakonnet Harbor Beach

items.name: Ship Pond Cove barrier beach

items.hours: Parking gate opens 8am; seasonal fee collection 8am-4pm approximately Memorial Day-Labor Day. Summer lifeguards. · Visitor parking $25 weekdays or $30 weekends/holidays; resident stickers available.

items.hours: Announced open houses and advance-booked private tours. · Open houses: no charge, donations encouraged. Private tours: 1–5 adults $75 total; 6+ adults $15 each; under 18 and members no charge.

items.name: Varnum House Museum
items.blurb: The historic house introduces the life and surroundings of James Mitchell Varnum. Public openings and private arrangements provide access to its museum rooms. Has: historic house, tours, appointments, event openings.
items.hours: Select Sundays 11 am–3 pm, designated town events and by appointment.

items.name: Crescent Park Looff Carousel
items.blurb: The surviving carousel preserves a major attraction from historic Crescent Park. The surrounding waterfront setting and carved ride make the site a living reminder of the area’s amusement-park past. Has: historic carousel, restrooms, concessions, seasonal operation.
items.address: 700 Bullocks Point Avenue, Riverside, East Providence
items.hours: Seasonal; operating times vary.

items.name: John Hunt House Museum / East Providence Historical Society
items.blurb: The Hunt House displays local-history collections beside the Ten Mile River. Docent-led open houses introduce East Providence’s people, industries and neighborhoods. Has: historic house, museum, docent tours, monthly open houses.
items.hours: Second Sunday of the month 1–3:30 pm.

items.name: Pomham Rocks Lighthouse
items.blurb: The restored lighthouse preserves rooms and objects illustrating life at a working navigational station. Guided boat visits include historical interpretation and an optional climb to the lantern room. Has: lighthouse museum, guided tours, boat access only, reservations, stairs, not wheelchair accessible, winter closure.
items.address: Pomham Rocks, Providence River; tour boats depart Edgewood Yacht Club in Cranston, East Providence
items.hours: Guided boat tours mid-June–September by reservation; closed for the current season. · Adults $50; current members $35; ages 6–17 $25; children under 6 not admitted.

items.name: Exeter Historical Association
items.blurb: The association works to preserve and share Exeter’s local history. A current public museum or research-visiting schedule was not verified. Has: historical association, public-access arrangements unconfirmed.

items.name: Tomaquag Museum
items.blurb: This Indigenous museum shares Native history, culture and contemporary perspectives. Public drop-in hours and reserved tours provide different ways to engage with its collections and educators. Has: Indigenous museum, guided programs, appointments, accessibility assistance.
items.hours: Wednesday 10 am–5 pm; Saturday 10 am–2 pm. Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday by booked tour; Sunday closed. · Adults $6; elders and college students $5; children $3; ages 5 and under no charge.

items.name: Borders Farm Museum and Historic Farm
items.blurb: A preserved working farm includes a farmhouse museum and an agricultural landscape. Public trails and scheduled programs connect visitors with rural life and the property’s history. Has: historic farm, farmhouse museum, trails, parking, portable toilet.
items.address: 31 North Road; trail parking at 38 North Road and Balcom Road, Foster
items.hours: Trails daily dawn–dusk; museum and event openings as announced.

items.name: Foster Town House / Foster Preservation Society
items.blurb: The society occupies the lower level of the historic town house. Visitors can explore local-history resources and arrange tours of the building. Has: historic town house, historical society, rear entrance, appointments.
items.hours: Wednesday 9 am–noon; other tours and visits by appointment.

items.name: Evans Schoolhouse
items.blurb: The restored one-room schoolhouse represents the rural district schools once used across Glocester. Its preservation allows the building to support interpretation of local educational history. Has: schoolhouse museum, special openings, current schedule unconfirmed.
items.address: Behind Glocester Town Hall, Putnam Pike
items.hours: Special public openings and educational programs; current dates unconfirmed.

items.name: Job Armstrong Store / Glocester Heritage Society
items.blurb: The restored store houses exhibits and the Glocester Heritage Society’s collections. Its visitor displays and archives interpret the community’s commercial and local history. Has: historic store, exhibits, archives, appointments.
items.hours: By appointment only.

items.name: Pettingill-Mason House / Dorr Rebellion Museum
items.blurb: The house served as a militia base during the Dorr Rebellion. Following restoration, it houses a museum devoted to that conflict and its local setting. Has: historic house, museum, Dorr Rebellion history.

items.name: Canonchet Brook Preserve
items.blurb: The preserve combines woodland habitat with stonework and remnants of earlier land use. Its trails offer access to a landscape shaped by Indigenous and colonial communities. Has: historic landscape, trails, leashed dogs, seasonal hunting precautions.
items.hours: Daylight hours year-round.

items.name: Hopkinton Historical Association Museum
items.blurb: The association preserves objects and records documenting Hopkinton’s families, villages and industries. Seasonal museum exhibitions complement its local-history and genealogy resources. Has: museum, historical association, genealogy, winter closure.
items.hours: Seasonal Sundays 10 am–2 pm; operator posts mid-May–mid-October. The 2026 sampler exhibition announced May 3–October 11.

items.name: Kenyon Crossroads Historic Site
items.blurb: Woodland trails pass the remains of an eighteenth-century settlement and historic road junction. Stone foundations and surviving landscape features help visitors imagine the former crossroads community. Has: outdoor historic site, trails, parking, year-round landscape.
items.address: Trail access from Woodville Road and Collins Road, Hopkinton
items.hours: Sunrise–sunset.

items.name: Beavertail Lighthouse Museum
items.blurb: The museum interprets the lighthouse and maritime history at the entrance to Narragansett Bay. Tower access is limited to announced climbing dates, with separate special openings late in the year. Has: lighthouse museum, scheduled tower climbs, gift shop, nearby public toilets.
items.hours: Seasonal museum; scheduled tower climbs. Group museum visits April 1–November 15 with at least two weeks notice; holiday shopping December 5–6 and 12–13, 2026, noon–3 pm. · Museum: no charge.

items.name: Conanicut Battery Historic Park
items.blurb: Surviving earthworks mark a coastal battery built during the Revolutionary War. Trails also introduce later military uses of the site and its commanding position over the bay. Has: fort earthworks, trails, outdoor historic site, year-round grounds.
items.hours: Daily sunrise–sunset.

items.name: Conanicut Friends Meetinghouse
items.blurb: The surviving Quaker meetinghouse reflects the island’s early religious community. Restoration has interrupted visits, and a current public-opening schedule needs confirmation. Has: historic meetinghouse, restoration, visitor access unconfirmed.
items.address: North Road and Weeden Lane, Jamestown
items.hours: Restoration closure announced for 2025; the proposed 2026 reopening was not confirmed.

items.name: Fort Burnside
items.blurb: The former coastal-defense installation preserves evidence of wartime surveillance at the bay entrance. Its disguised control post and battery landscape can be explored through public park areas and arranged interpretation. Has: fort, military museum, outdoor remains, appointments, year-round grounds.
items.address: Beavertail Road, Beavertail State Park, Jamestown
items.hours: Park grounds daily sunrise–sunset; museum and building access by appointment or scheduled programs. · Park grounds and parking: no charge.

items.name: Fort Getty Park
items.blurb: Historic fortifications survive within this town park overlooking the bay. Public park access combines views of the military remains with shoreline and walking areas. Has: fort remains, park, walking trail, parking, seasonal camping.
items.address: End of Fort Getty Road, Jamestown
items.hours: Park 7 am–10 pm; campground seasonal and currently closed for camping. · Summer daily parking $20; parking with boat $30; resident and seasonal passes available.

items.name: Fort Wetherill State Park
items.blurb: This former coastal-defense installation occupies granite cliffs overlooking Narragansett Bay. Visitors can explore the public park landscape and view surviving military structures. Has: fort, outdoor historic site, coastal views, trails.

items.name: Jamestown Fire Department Memorial Museum
items.blurb: The fire department’s museum preserves material associated with local firefighting. Its building stands beside the main station, but current visitor hours need confirmation. Has: fire museum, access schedule unconfirmed.

items.name: Jamestown Historical Society Museum
items.blurb: Local-history exhibitions occupy a former one-room schoolhouse that later served as the town library. The building has an accessible entrance and welcomes special visit requests. Has: museum, accessible, seasonal exhibitions, appointments.
items.hours: May 22–October 12, 2026: Friday–Sunday and holidays 1–4 pm; visits by appointment outside regular hours.

items.name: Jamestown Town Pound
items.blurb: The stone enclosure once held stray farm animals until their owners reclaimed them. Interpretive signage explains the history of animal pounds on the island. Has: outdoor historic site, interpretive signs, roadside parking, winter access.
items.address: East side of North Road, north of Route 138, Jamestown
items.hours: Daylight hours year-round.

items.name: Jamestown Windmill
items.blurb: This surviving windmill illustrates the island’s agricultural and milling history. Visitors can inspect the historic structure during seasonal openings or arrange a visit. Has: windmill, tours, parking, stairs, not wheelchair accessible.
items.hours: May 22–October 12, 2026: Friday–Sunday and holidays 1–4 pm, weather permitting; also by appointment. · No charge; donations welcome.

items.name: Watson Farm
items.blurb: A working coastal farm preserves a landscape shaped by generations of agricultural use. Self-guided walks pass livestock and fields, while the farmhouse remains a private residence viewed only from outside. Has: historic farm, self-guided walks, parking, farmhouse exterior only.

items.name: Clemence-Irons House
items.blurb: This rare stone-ender house preserves evidence of early Rhode Island construction and later restoration. Guided tours explain both the building’s long occupancy and its twentieth-century reconstruction. Has: guided tours, historic house, street parking, stairs, no public restroom.

items.blurb: A historic house and museum barn hold Johnston’s local-history collections. The house’s first floor is maintained as a museum, with artifacts and archives in the rear building. Has: historic house, museum barn, archives, appointments.
items.hours: Tuesday 6:30–8:30 pm; Thursday 9 am–noon; also by appointment.

items.name: Arnold House
items.blurb: The seventeenth-century stone-ender combines a massive masonry end wall with surviving timber construction. Tours trace the house’s use, alteration and restoration over several centuries. Has: guided tours, historic house, parking at Gateway Park, stairs, seasonal opening.
items.hours: Sundays June–early October; hourly tours 11 am–3 pm, last tour 3 pm. · Adults $10; seniors $9; students and children $5; members no charge.

items.name: Arnold's Lonsdale Bakery
items.blurb: The historic bakery building preserves a part of the Blackstone Valley’s commercial life. Special open days connect it with the nearby toll house and the society’s historical interpretation. Has: historic bakery, special openings, historical society campus.

items.blurb: Exhibits in the former canal captain’s house explain transportation changes in the Blackstone Valley. The surrounding park connects the museum with surviving canal and industrial landscapes. Has: museum, historic house, parking, accessible with uneven areas, winter exterior access.
items.hours: Seasonal spring–October; DEM posts 9 am–5 pm except Friday. Grounds dawn–dusk year-round; confirm museum dates because agency schedules differ. · No charge.

items.name: Hannaway Blacksmith Shop
items.blurb: The relocated shop preserves equipment and skills associated with traditional blacksmithing. Demonstrations and small classes bring the historic forge into use. Has: historic workshop, demonstrations, advance class booking, winter programs.
items.address: Great Road Heritage Campus, Chase Farm Park, Lincoln
items.hours: Classes and demonstrations on published calendar dates year-round; advance booking for classes.

items.name: Hearthside House
items.blurb: The stone mansion presents furnished rooms and changing historical programs. Costumed docents interpret the families who lived there and the community around Great Road. Has: historic mansion, guided tours, period furnishings, scheduled programs.
items.hours: Scheduled tour and program dates only; no regular daily schedule.

items.name: Hearthside House / Great Road Heritage Campus
items.blurb: Historic-house interpretation and related heritage buildings presented through scheduled tours and programs.

items.blurb: This early machine shop retains tools and equipment from its working life. Supervised visits interpret the varied products once made for local farms and businesses. Has: historic mill, machinery, shuttle access only, seasonal closure.

items.hours: Closed for the 2026 season; access only by shuttle on scheduled campus tour dates.

items.name: North Gate Toll House / Blackstone Valley Historical Society
items.blurb: The former toll house houses historical collections associated with the Blackstone Valley. Exhibits and public programs connect the building with local roads, communities and industry. Has: historic house, historical society, museum collections, event-based access.
items.hours: Announced public programs and special openings.

items.blurb: The restored one-room schoolhouse recalls education in a rural nineteenth-century community. It was moved to Chase Farm Park and reopened for visitors and educational groups. Has: schoolhouse, educational programs, calendar-based openings.
items.hours: Scheduled open houses, school visits and campus programs.

items.name: Wilbor House Museum / Little Compton Historical Society
items.blurb: The Wilbor House and surrounding museum campus interpret Little Compton’s people and domestic life. Guided house tours and self-guided exhibits follow different seasonal schedules. Has: historic house, exhibits, outbuildings, winter weekday access, house tours by appointment.

items.blurb: The restored windmill illustrates Middletown’s agricultural and milling heritage. Seasonal docent visits supplement outdoor interpretation available in Paradise Park. Has: windmill, guided tours, parking, exterior year-round.

items.hours: 2026 summer: Sunday 2–4 pm; interior visits seasonal; park and exterior interpretation year-round.

items.name: Paradise School Museum / Middletown Historical Society
items.blurb: The historic schoolhouse contains the society’s museum, archives and main office. Its collections interpret Middletown and the landscape around Paradise Valley. Has: schoolhouse museum, archives, adjacent park, seasonal schedule.
items.address: Paradise Avenue and Prospect Avenue, Middletown
items.hours: 2026 summer: Sunday 2–4 pm and Wednesday 9–11 am; office hours vary seasonally.

items.name: Prescott Farm
items.blurb: This historic landscape includes a windmill and agricultural outbuildings. Visitors can explore the public grounds while respecting marked private areas. Has: historic farm, windmill, outdoor exploration, grounds year-round.
items.hours: Daily dawn–dusk. · Grounds: no charge.

items.name: Whitehall Museum House
items.blurb: The former home of philosopher George Berkeley preserves an early eighteenth-century domestic setting. Its architecture and interpretation explore Berkeley’s brief residence on Aquidneck Island. Has: historic house, tours, seasonal opening, winter closure.

items.name: Witherbee School

items.hours: Selected summer Sundays 2–4 pm; seasonal opening only.

items.name: Narragansett Historical Society
items.blurb: The society documents Narragansett’s buildings, neighborhoods and community history. Its public activities include historical programs, walking tours and resources for exploring the town independently. Has: historical society, walking tours, public programs.
items.hours: Public programs and walking tours on announced dates; no regular museum hours published.

items.name: South County Museum
items.blurb: An outdoor museum campus explores the region’s farming, coastal trades and village life. Historic craft shops, agricultural displays and remnants of the Canonchet estate connect artifacts with the landscape. Has: living history, craft demonstrations, farm animals, trails, seasonal buildings.
items.hours: Regular 2026 season ended; special events and classes continue. In-season published hours: Thursday–Saturday 10 am–4 pm, last admission 3 pm. · Adults $12; seniors and students $10; children over six $5; members no charge.

items.name: The Towers

Historical interpretation and public music, dance and cultural events give visitors access to the restored landmark. Has: historic casino remains, history gallery, public events, summer tours, accessible.
items.hours: Public events on announced dates; summer tours offered; regular gallery hours not verified.

items.name: Block Island Historical Society Museum
items.blurb: The museum occupies a former home and summer hotel in the Old Harbor district. Collections trace Indigenous history, maritime work, farming and the island’s visitor economy. Has: museum, historic building, gallery, gift shop, seasonal holiday opening.
items.hours: Closed for regular 2026 season; reopening for Holiday Stroll weekend beginning November 27. Summer daily 10 am–4 pm; shoulder seasons Friday–Monday 10 am–2 pm.

items.name: Block Island North Light Maritime Museum

items.address: North end of Corn Neck Road, New Shoreham
items.hours: Posted seasonal hours: Saturday 10 am–4 pm; Sunday noon–4 pm; Columbus Day 10 am–4 pm. Closed after Columbus Day and during rain. · Ages 12 and over $3.

items.name: Block Island Southeast Lighthouse Museum
items.blurb: The lighthouse museum interprets an important navigation landmark and its relocation away from the eroding bluff. Guided tower tours provide an additional way to experience the structure. Has: lighthouse museum, guided tower tours, grounds year-round, winter interior closure.
items.hours: Spring May 24–June 22 weekends 10 am–4 pm; summer through Labor Day daily 10 am–4 pm; fall through October 12 weekends 10 am–4 pm. items.name: Artillery Company of Newport Museum

items.name: Audrain Automobile Museum
items.blurb: Rotating exhibitions present rare vehicles from different periods of automotive history. The museum emphasizes the relationship between design, technology and the automobile. Has: automobile museum, changing exhibitions, winter hours.
items.hours: Daily 10 am–4 pm. · Adults $18; seniors 65+, military and students with ID $10; ages 6–17 $8; members no charge.

items.name: Belcourt of Newport

items.name: Chateau-sur-Mer
items.blurb: The house preserves a richly layered example of Victorian design and decoration. Audio and landscape tours explore the Wetmore family’s residence and grounds. Has: mansion, audio tours, parking, not wheelchair accessible, winter weekend openings.
items.hours: Closed until November 21, 2026; then Saturday–Sunday 9 am–5 pm through January 3, 2027, last admission 4 pm. · One-property admission: adults $25; ages 6–12 $10; under 6 no charge.

items.name: Chepstow
items.blurb: This summer residence preserves Morris-Gallatin furnishings and American art. Guided visits explore its collections and the family history reflected in its rooms. Has: guided tours, timed tickets, parking, not wheelchair accessible, seasonal opening.
items.hours: Closed for the 2026 season; next regular opening dates not published on the reviewed page.

items.name: Common Burying Ground and God's Little Acre
items.blurb: The colonial burying ground preserves carved gravestones and evidence of Newport’s early communities. items.hours: Daily 7 am–sunset.

items.name: Fort Adams
items.blurb: The coastal fort interprets the military defenses guarding Newport Harbor. Guided and self-guided visits reveal its engineering, buildings and waterfront position. Has: fort, guided tours, self-guided visits, seasonal tour schedule.
items.hours: Daily April–November; visitor center 9 am–4 pm; tour times vary with season, weather and events. · Admission starts at $10.

items.name: Fort Adams Interior Tours
items.blurb: Guided or self-guided exploration of the coastal fortress, with access determined by the selected tour.

items.hours: Site tours on a limited basis, subject to guide and building availability.

items.name: Hunter House

items.hours: Closed for the 2026 season; next regular opening dates not published on the reviewed page.

items.hours: Daily 10 am–5 pm, last admission 4:30 pm; closed Thanksgiving and December 24–25, 2026. Selected guided tours Friday and Sunday; event exceptions apply. · Adults $25; seniors, military, students and USTA members $21.50; ages 12 and under no charge.

items.name: Isaac Bell House
items.blurb: This Shingle Style house emphasizes architectural design and craftsmanship. Sparsely furnished interiors make its materials and spatial arrangement central to the visit. Has: historic house, architecture, parking, not wheelchair accessible, seasonal opening.
items.hours: Closed for the 2026 season; next regular opening dates not published on the reviewed page. · One-property admission: adults $25; ages 6–12 $10; under 6 no charge.

items.name: Kings Cote / Kingscote

items.hours: Closed for the 2026 season; next regular opening dates not published on the reviewed page. · One-property admission: adults $25; ages 6–12 $10; under 6 no charge.

items.hours: November 2026–January 3, 2027: daily 9 am–5 pm, last entry 4 pm; December 24 closes 2 pm; closed Thanksgiving and Christmas. · One-property admission: adults $25; ages 6–12 $10; under 6 no charge.

items.hours: Regular 2026 season May 22–October 25: Thursday–Sunday noon–5 pm; off-season visits by arrangement.

items.name: Naval War College Museum

items.name: Newport Art Museum / John N. A. Griswold House

items.hours: Wednesday–Monday 11 am–4 pm; Tuesday closed. Closed New Year’s Eve, New Year’s Day, Easter, Thanksgiving, Christmas Eve and Christmas Day. · Adults $20; seniors 65+ $15; college students $10; members, ages 17 and under, active military and spouse no charge.

items.name: Newport Colony House
items.blurb: The former colonial government building preserves an important chapter of Rhode Island civic history. Limited tours and programs introduce its architecture and public uses. Has: historic building, limited site tours, advance inquiry.

items.name: Newport Tower Museum

items.hours: Closed for the 2026 season; next regular opening dates not published on the reviewed page.

items.name: The Elms
items.blurb: A mansion with formal gardens and historic household technology. Note: The operator announces reopening November 16, 2026, with a new timed-ticket experience.

items.name: The Sailing Museum and National Sailing Hall of Fame
items.blurb: Interactive exhibits explore sailing through its people, techniques and history. Hall of Fame displays recognize contributors to the sport alongside broader maritime interpretation. Has: maritime museum, interactive exhibits, sports history, winter hours.
items.hours: Daily 10 am–5 pm, last admission 4:15 pm. Closes 3 pm November 25, December 24 and December 31; closed Thanksgiving and Christmas. · Adults $20; ages 11–17 $15; ages 5–10 $8; under 5 no charge.

items.name: Touro Synagogue
items.blurb: Guided tours interpret the historic synagogue and Newport’s Jewish community. The building remains an active place of worship, so visitor access follows a separate reservation calendar. Has: historic synagogue, guided tours, reservations required, no on-site parking, no public restroom, not wheelchair accessible.
items.hours: Reserved public tours on published dates. Winter dates include December 13, 20 and 27, 2026, and January 3 and 17, 2027, at 11:30 am and 12:45 pm; no Sabbath or major religious-holiday tours. · Adults $18; seniors 65+ and children under 13 $10.

items.name: Trinity Church and Historic Graveyard
items.blurb: The historic church preserves an eighteenth-century worship space in central Newport. Church and graveyard tours connect its architecture with the people of the colonial town. Has: historic church, graveyard, tours, accessible, limited restrooms, winter Sunday tours.
items.hours: Sunday 11:30 am–12:30 pm year-round; April–Memorial Day also Friday–Saturday 10 am–4 pm; Memorial Day–October Monday–Saturday 10 am–4 pm. Additional winter holiday dates announced separately; private tours by appointment. · Suggested donation $5; children no charge. Private tours $5 per person, minimum $50.

items.name: Vernon House
items.blurb: This early Newport house is used for exhibitions, public dialogue and preservation learning. Its architectural fabric and surviving decorative panels support ongoing interpretation of the building’s past. Has: historic house, exhibitions, stairs to upper floors, seasonal access.
items.hours: October 3–November 22, 2026: Tuesday–Sunday 10 am–5 pm; other programs and private visits by arrangement. · No charge for the announced exhibition.

items.name: Wanton-Lyman-Hazard House
items.blurb: One of Newport’s oldest surviving houses preserves evidence of several prominent households. Its interpretation connects domestic life with the city’s colonial history. Has: historic building, limited site tours, advance inquiry.
items.hours: Site tours on a limited basis, subject to guide and building availability.

items.name: Casey Farm
items.blurb: This historic farm combines an agricultural landscape with a farmhouse museum gallery. Guided visits address the lives of the people who owned and worked the property, including enslaved people and tenant farmers. Has: guided tours, historic farm, parking, unpaved paths, seasonal market.
items.address: 2325 Boston Neck Road, Saunderstown, North Kingstown
items.hours: Farm tours: Saturdays May 16–October 31 at 9, 10 and 11 am; Tuesdays June–October 15 at 1, 2 and 3 pm. Market: Saturdays mid-May–October 8:30 am–12:30 pm. · Tours: adults $10; seniors $9; students and children $5; family $25; members and North Kingstown residents no charge.

items.name: Gilbert Stuart Birthplace and Museum
items.blurb: The restored Stuart family home introduces the life of the portrait painter Gilbert Stuart. The property also offers gardens, woodland trails and a historic millpond setting. Has: historic house, museum, gardens, trails, winter closure.
items.address: 815 Gilbert Stuart Road, Saunderstown, North Kingstown
items.hours: April 29–October 25, 2026: Wednesday–Sunday 10 am–4 pm. Closed October 26, 2026–April 28, 2027. · Adults $15; children 6–12 $8; members no charge.

items.name: Old Narragansett Church
items.blurb: The surviving colonial church retains a distinctive historic interior. Summer tours interpret its architecture and the congregation’s long history in the region. Has: historic church, docent tours, seasonal access.
items.hours: Docent-led tours during summer; special events separately scheduled. Winter routine tour hours not published.

items.name: Rhode Island Computer Museum
items.blurb: The museum preserves computers and related technology as evidence of the information age. Exhibits and educational activities connect older machines with the ways people learned, worked and communicated. Has: technology museum, educational programs, winter hours.
items.hours: Tuesday and Friday noon–4 pm; Saturday 10 am–5 pm; Sunday noon–4 pm.

items.name: Seabee Museum & Memorial Park
items.blurb: Quonset huts, artifacts, and exhibits at the original Rhode Island home of the Navy’s Seabees.

items.name: Seabee Museum and Memorial Park
items.blurb: Quonset huts, artifacts and memorials tell the story of the Navy’s construction battalions at their original Rhode Island base. Group visits can be tailored to students, veterans and other visitors. Has: military museum, memorial park, Quonset huts, accessible parking, group tours.
items.hours: Wednesday, Friday and Saturday 9:30 am–2 pm; other days closed.

items.name: Smith's Castle
items.blurb: Docent-led tours interpret this early house and the layered history of Cocumscussoc. The site addresses Indigenous history, colonial settlement and enslavement as well as the surviving building. Has: guided tours only, historic house, gardens, seasonal tours, winter special events.
items.hours: May and October: Saturday–Sunday tours noon, 1, 2 and 3 pm; June–September: Friday–Sunday at those times. Regular 2026 tour season ended; fall and winter special events continue. · Adults $10; seniors and military $8; children 6–12 $5; ages 5 and under no charge.

items.name: Old North Providence Town Hall
items.blurb: The town identifies its former town hall as a protected historic building. A current public interior-visiting schedule was not verified, so access needs confirmation. Has: historic civic building, public interior access unconfirmed.

items.name: Forestdale Schoolhouse / North Smithfield Heritage Association
items.blurb: The restored schoolhouse contains the heritage association’s museum and local school-history resources. Its exhibits and research collections introduce North Smithfield’s communities and educational past. Has: schoolhouse museum, historical association, gift shop, monthly opening.
items.hours: Second and third Thursday and Saturday of each month 10 am–3 pm; call before traveling.

items.name: Heritage Hall
items.blurb: The restored former grange hall hosts historical and cultural programs. Special exhibitions and regular presentations provide public access to the community building. Has: historic grange hall, historical programs, occasional exhibitions, winter programs.
items.hours: History Nights third Friday of each month at 7 pm; additional exhibitions and programs on announced dates.

items.name: Memorial Town Building / North Smithfield Heritage Association Archives
items.blurb: The former town hall was built as a memorial to residents who served in the First World War. It now houses the heritage association’s archives, research center and headquarters. Has: historic civic building, historical association, archives, winter hours.
items.hours: Monday and Wednesday 10 am–noon; Tuesday 9 am–noon.

items.name: Slatersville Historic Mill Village
items.blurb: The planned mill village preserves the relationship between factories, housing and community spaces. A National Park Service walking route explains how its layout influenced later industrial settlements. Has: historic district, self-guided tour, interpretive information, exterior access.
items.address: Self-guided tour begins at 20 Main Street, Slatersville, North Smithfield
items.hours: Self-guided exterior walking route on public sidewalks and paths.

items.name: Cape Verdean Museum
items.blurb: The museum explores Cape Verdean history and the community’s experience in the United States. Photographs, documents and objects connect island life, migration and cultural traditions. Has: museum, cultural history, research resources.
items.hours: Group visits can be arranged by email; current weekly opening times not verified.

items.name: Daggett House Museum
items.blurb: The early house survives within Slater Park as a museum of local domestic history. Announced heritage events provide opportunities to visit its historic rooms. Has: historic house, museum, special-event tours, park setting.
items.address: Slater Memorial Park, Newport Avenue, Pawtucket
items.hours: Public tours during announced heritage events; regular schedule not verified.

items.name: Old Slater Mill
items.blurb: National Park Service interpretation of early textile manufacturing and the changes brought by industrialization. Note: Tour seasons vary; neighboring historic buildings may have separate closures.

items.name: Old Slater Mill National Historic Landmark
items.blurb: The historic cotton-spinning mill interprets the industrial transformation of the Blackstone Valley. Ranger tours and exhibits explain the machinery, labor and investment behind early manufacturing. Has: historic mill, ranger tours, parking, accessible entrance, winter interior closure.
items.hours: November 1–28, 2026: Friday–Saturday 10 am–4 pm; tours 10:30 am, 12:30 pm and 2:30 pm. Interior winter closure November 29–April 23; grounds daily dawn–dusk. · No charge.

items.name: Rhode Island Music Hall of Fame
items.blurb: Displays honor musicians and other people who helped shape Rhode Island’s musical life. The public exhibition occupies a hallway inside the former mill complex at Hope Artiste Village. Has: music history, museum displays, historic mill building, winter hours.
items.address: Hope Artiste Village, 999 Main Street, Pawtucket
items.hours: Daily 9 am–5 pm. · No charge.

items.name: Slater Park Looff Carousel
items.blurb: The surviving wooden carousel preserves the work of historic carousel maker Charles Looff. Seasonal rides allow visitors to experience an amusement associated with generations of parkgoers. Has: historic carousel, seasonal rides, park setting, winter closure.
items.address: Slater Memorial Park, Armistice Boulevard, Pawtucket
items.hours: Seasonal April–October; daily during the main summer season and weekends in spring and fall. Posted weekend hours 11 am–4:45 pm; confirm current dates.

items.name: Sylvanus Brown House
items.blurb: The historic house stands within the Slater Mill campus. Its exterior remains visible from the grounds while interior visits are suspended. Has: historic house, exterior viewing, interior closed.
items.hours: Interior closed pending safety and accessibility work; surrounding grounds daily dawn–dusk. · Grounds: no charge.

items.name: Wilkinson Mill
items.blurb: This industrial building forms part of the Slater Mill historic campus. Visitors can view its exterior from public grounds while interior access remains suspended. Has: historic mill, exterior viewing, interior closed.
items.hours: Interior closed pending safety and accessibility work; surrounding grounds daily dawn–dusk. · Grounds: no charge.

items.name: Butts Hill Fort
items.blurb: Earthworks survive from a Revolutionary War fort associated with the Battle of Rhode Island. Public paths provide access to the site and its defensive landscape. Has: fort earthworks, outdoor historic site, walking paths, parking restrictions near school.
items.address: Dyer Street, off Sprague Street, Portsmouth

items.name: Green Animals Topiary Garden
items.blurb: The historic garden contains carefully maintained topiary figures and seasonal flower displays. Its bayfront landscape preserves a distinctive tradition of ornamental gardening. Has: historic garden, topiary, parking, not wheelchair accessible, winter closure.
items.hours: Closed for the 2026 season; next opening dates not published on the reviewed page. · One-property admission: adults $25; ages 6–12 $10; under 6 no charge.

items.name: Newport Car Museum
items.blurb: The museum presents automobiles as examples of engineering and industrial design. Themed galleries trace changing styles and performance across different periods of motoring history. Has: automobile museum, galleries, winter hours.
items.hours: Daily 10 am–5 pm; closed Thanksgiving, Christmas and New Year’s Day; closes 2 pm on their preceding days. · Adults $20; seniors, military and students $17; children 5–12 $10.

items.name: Portsmouth Historical Society Museum, Southermost Schoolhouse and Old Town Hall
items.blurb: The former Christian Union Church houses Portsmouth’s local-history museum. The society also preserves an early schoolhouse and the old town hall at its historic campus. Has: museum, historic church, schoolhouse, town hall, winter appointments.
items.address: East Main Road and Union Street, Portsmouth
items.hours: Closed for winter except special events; private tours and research visits by arrangement. · Suggested donation $5 per nonmember; members no charge.

items.name: Prudence Island Historical Museum
items.blurb: The island museum preserves objects and records connected with Prudence Island’s past. Its displays place local families and island activities within Narragansett Bay history. Has: island museum, accessible, street parking, ferry travel required, schedule unconfirmed.

items.name: Aldrich House
items.blurb: The historic house serves as the headquarters of the Rhode Island Historical Society. Arranged visits and public programs offer access to a building associated with the Aldrich family. Has: historic house, historical society headquarters, accessible, appointments.
items.hours: By appointment and for announced Rhode Island Historical Society events and programs.

items.name: Annmary Brown Memorial
items.blurb: This university memorial combines an art gallery, historical collections and a mausoleum. Displays include European and American paintings and personal material associated with its founders. Has: art collection, historic memorial, access schedule unconfirmed.

items.name: First Baptist Church in America
items.blurb: The historic meetinghouse interprets the congregation’s place in Providence and religious history. Public tours introduce the building while it continues to serve an active congregation. Has: historic church, tours, reservations for groups, winter tours.
items.hours: Tours Tuesday and Thursday at noon, 12:30, 1 and 1:30 pm; Sunday after worship, approximately 12:15 pm September–May and 11:15 am June–August. Group visits by reservation.

items.name: John Carter Brown Library Exhibition Gallery
items.blurb: Exhibitions draw on rare books, maps and manuscripts concerning the early Americas. The historic research library offers a broader view of colonial and revolutionary history across the hemisphere. Has: historic library, historical exhibitions, research appointments, winter hours.
items.hours: Monday–Thursday 10 am–12:45 pm and 2–4:45 pm; Friday 10 am–12:45 pm. Research seats require appointments. · Exhibitions: no charge.

items.name: John Hay Library Exhibition Gallery and Special Collections

items.name: Ladd Observatory

items.hours: Tuesday public evenings, weather permitting, with advance tickets; current sessions 7–9 pm. Closed November 3, 2026; next scheduled opening November 10. · No charge; reservation required.

items.name: Lippitt House Museum

items.name: Mary Elizabeth Robinson Research Center / Rhode Island Historical Society
items.blurb: The research center provides public access to Rhode Island historical and genealogical collections. items.hours: Reading room Wednesday–Friday; consult current calendar for daily times and occasional Saturday openings. Manuscripts and selected collections by appointment. · Reading-room admission currently waived; no charge. Separate collection-research services may have fees.

items.hours: Tuesday–Thursday 1–4 pm; Friday–Saturday 10 am–4 pm. December 1–March: Friday–Saturday only 10 am–4 pm; closed Thanksgiving, December 24–25, December 31 and January 1. · Adults $10; seniors 62+, veterans and students $8; children under 10, members and eligible EBT parties no charge.

items.name: Museum of Natural History and Planetarium

items.hours: Museum daily 10 am–4 pm, last admission 3:30 pm; planetarium generally Saturday–Sunday 2 pm. Museum closes at 1 pm November 9 and December 7; holiday closures listed online. · Museum $2; children under 4 and members no charge. Planetarium $5 including museum; minimum age 4.

items.name: North Burial Ground

items.name: Old Brick School House / Providence Preservation Society

It later became the preservation society’s headquarters, although current walk-in interior access was not verified. Has: historic schoolhouse, preservation organization, public interior access unconfirmed.

items.name: Old State House

items.hours: Tours by arrangement; not open for daily historic-site tours.

items.name: Providence Athenaeum

items.name: Rhode Island Black Heritage Society

items.name: Rhode Island State Archives

items.hours: Monday–Friday 8:30 am–4:30 pm. · No charge.

items.name: Rhode Island State House

items.name: RISD Museum

items.name: Roger Williams National Memorial and Antram-Gray House Visitor Center
items.blurb: The memorial interprets Roger Williams and his influence on religious liberty. Exhibits in a historic house complement outdoor interpretive panels and landscaped grounds. Has: historic site, visitor-center exhibits, outdoor interpretation, parking.
items.hours: Grounds daily dawn–dusk; visitor center Thursday–Sunday 10 am–4 pm; closed Thanksgiving, Christmas and New Year’s Day.

items.name: Sandra Bornstein Holocaust Education Center
items.blurb: The center uses historical resources and educational programs to teach about the Holocaust. Its work connects survivor testimony and documented history with public learning. Has: historical education, collections, programs, winter hours.

items.name: Shakespeare's Head House and Garden
items.blurb: The former home and workplace of printer John Carter connects Providence’s publishing and postal history. Its garden remains accessible while the house is prepared for a new public-history use. Has: historic house, public garden, house interior closed, winter garden access.

items.name: Stephen Hopkins House

items.hours: Closed for the 2026 season; interior painting planned over winter; reopening expected spring 2027.

items.name: Swan Point Cemetery

items.hours: Grounds April 1–September 30 daily 8 am–7 pm; October 1–March 31 daily 8 am–5 pm, conditions permitting.

items.name: The Museum at the John Brown House
items.blurb: A historic house used to explore Rhode Island’s social, commercial, and family history.

items.name: Richmond Historical Society Archives

items.name: Scituate Preservation Society
items.blurb: The society preserves and interprets historical and cultural material relating to Scituate. Its public educational work is documented, but a current drop-in museum schedule was not verified. Has: historical society, local-history collections, public access schedule unconfirmed.

items.name: Smith-Appleby House Museum / Historical Society of Smithfield

items.name: Fayerweather House

items.name: South County History Center / Old Washington County Jail

items.name: University of Rhode Island Textile Gallery and Historic Textile Collection
items.blurb: The university’s textile collection preserves clothing and fabrics used for research and teaching. Public gallery exhibitions introduce aspects of dress, design and material history. Has: textile museum collection, changing exhibitions, academic-year hours, appointments.

items.name: Chace-Cory House / Tiverton Historical Society

items.name: Clouds Hill Museum
